ideas.name: AAO-Cap: self-ordered anodic-alumina capacitor mold
ideas.one_liner: Grow the DRAM capacitor holes by anodizing an aluminum film whose pores self-organize, imprint-registered to the transistors, instead of plasma-etching 60:1 holes in SiO2 with fluorocarbons.
ideas.mechanism: Sputter a 2.5-3 um Al film over the access-transistor array and its TiN/W landing pads. Nanoimprint shallow pits registered to the pads (Masuda pretexturing), then anodize at ~15-20 V in sulfuric/oxalic acid: pores nucleate at the pits and grow straight down at aspect ratio >=100, stopping at the pad metal; the alumina barrier at each pore bottom is thinned by a voltage ramp-down and removed by a short wet or atomic-layer etch. An ALD Al2O3 liner seals the anion-contaminated pore walls, then TiN / ZrO2-Al2O3-ZrO2 (or the B2-02/B2-03 dielectric) / TiN cup capacitors are ALD-coated inside the pores. The rigid alumina honeycomb stays in place as the mechanical support lattice, so there is no pillar leaning and no SiN support-lattice masks. The bit is stored and sensed exactly as in a 1T1C cell (Si BCAT or IGZO 4F2 VCT access device).
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 storage-capacitor charge wall (HAR etch, leaning/collapse) and A1 #4 capital/masks of the capacitor module; A2 PFAS/fluorocarbon chokepoint (the C4F6/C4F8 HAR SiO2 etch).
ideas.step_change_claim: Capacitor 2.5-3 um tall (pore AR ~100-115) with no plasma HAR etch: Cs 7.4-8.9 fF at a 4F2 40 nm-pitch cell (+37-64% vs 1-beta's 5.4 fF) at ~1-beta-parity density with periphery under cell; capacitor-hole module goes from ~3 masks + fluorocarbon HAR etch + SiN lattice to 1 imprint + wet anodization (~8 Wh/wafer).
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-01: 4F2 at F=20 nm -> 40 nm square pitch (the bottom of AAO's demonstrated 40-500 nm interval). Pore widened to 26 nm (porosity 0.33); after a 3 nm TiN liner and a ~5 nm dielectric the mid-plane diameter is ~15 nm. C = 3.9*eps0*pi*d*h/EOT with EOT 0.55 nm: h=2.5 um -> 7.40 fF; 3.0 um -> 8.88 fF (1-beta pillar 21 nm x 1.3 um -> 5.38 fF, matches A1). Density 4F2 F=20 nm: 0.319 Gb/mm2 at array eff 0.51 (0.71x 1-beta), 0.438 Gb/mm2 with periphery-under-cell eff 0.70 (0.98x). Anodization: 0.19 g Al/wafer, 2,011 C, 8.4 Wh at 15 V vs ~1,300 kWh/wafer fab total (A2). Scaling check: UMD AAO capacitance rises ~linearly with pore depth (11 -> 26 uF/cm2 from 1 to 2 um).

ideas.novelty: TWIST on known: ALD MIM nanocapacitors in AAO (UMD/Rubloff 2009) and imprint-ordered AAO (Masuda) are known for energy storage and templates; using registered AAO as the DRAM cell-capacitor mold with the alumina walls as the permanent support lattice is a NEW combination (no DRAM use found).
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Pitch: ideally ordered AAO is reported at 40-500 nm intervals; today's 1-beta/1c honeycomb is 32-35 nm, at or beyond the edge. (2) Removing the alumina barrier at the bottom of 20-26 nm pores without attacking the landing pad, with imprint-to-pad overlay of ~3-4 nm. (3) Electrolyte anions and charge in AAO walls (and pore branching at Al grain boundaries) add leakage, traps and defects.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Target 4F2 at F=20 nm (40 nm pitch), where AAO is demonstrated, and get density from 4F2 plus periphery-under-cell rather than pitch; Kondo-style mold-interval reduction for later shrinks; Cs scales with height, so 3-4 um pores buy margin. (2) Anodize onto a thin valve-metal stop layer (Ti/Nb) that converts to a removable oxide; voltage ramp-down barrier thinning; self-aligned landing pads (B2-14) relax overlay. (3) ALD Al2O3 passivation liner (UMD needed it for leakage) plus <=450 C anneal; large-grain or Al-Cu films; residual defects absorbed by repair/ECC (B2-15).
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 18 months, ~$350k of the $1M: sputter Al on 100-150 mm wafers with TiN pad arrays at 40-60 nm pitch (e-beam-written pads), imprint-pretexture and anodize; SEM-map ordering and pore-bottom opening defects over mm2 areas (~$120k of nanofab time). ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN in the pores; measure C, J at 0.5 V (target <=1e-7 A/cm2), breakdown and per-capacitor C spread with small addressable test arrays (~$130k). Integrate 64x64 1T1C cells using a university IGZO TFT layer under the AAO (~$100k).
ideas.resource_angle: Removes the fluorocarbon (PFAS-class, high-GWP) HAR etch and the SiN lattice from the capacitor module; Al is abundant (0.19 g/wafer); room-temperature wet electrochemistry at ~8 Wh/wafer; fewer plasma-etch hours (less helium-cooled chuck time); no EUV.

ideas.name: Ru-free rutile: SnO2-templated TiO2 short-stub capacitor
ideas.one_liner: Get k 60-100 rutile TiO2 at 250-340 C by growing it on abundant, conductive, rutile-structured doped SnO2 instead of scarce Ru/RuO2, and spend the gain on a much shorter capacitor.
ideas.mechanism: Cap the TiN bottom electrode with 3-5 nm of ALD Ta-, Nb- or F-doped SnO2 (conductive, rutile/cassiterite structure, a=4.74 A vs rutile TiO2 a=4.59 A). ALD TiO2 (optionally lightly Al-doped to suppress leakage) nucleates epitaxially in the rutile phase on the SnO2 grains at 250-340 C, giving k ~60-100 without the >800 C anneal or the Ru/RuO2 template used in earlier rutile work. A doped-SnO2 top electrode makes the stack symmetric and keeps the high-work-function contact. At 7 nm physical thickness the EOT is 0.34-0.40 nm. The capacitor is used either to shorten the 1-beta pillar from 1.3 um to 0.8-0.95 um, or as a 0.30-0.35 um stub holding ~2 fF for short-bitline, 4F2 or 3D-tier cells.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 capacitor wall (k>60 needed) and A1 #2 (a capacitor that fits a 3D tier); A2 warning that Ru electrodes fleet-wide need 26-176% of world Ru and HZO needs 14-41% of separated Hf.
ideas.step_change_claim: 1.4-1.6x more capacitance per area than ZrO2-based stacks (EOT 0.40/0.34 vs 0.55 nm): equal Cs from a capacitor 27-38% shorter (AR ~39-45 instead of 62), or 2 fF from a 0.30-0.35 um stub; zero Ru and zero Hf.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-02: k=68 (Gordon 2010) at 7 nm -> EOT 0.401 nm -> h(5.4 fF, d=21 nm)=0.95 um, h(2.0 fF)=0.35 um; k=80 -> 0.81/0.30 um; k=100 -> 0.65/0.24 um. Leakage budget: sidewall area of the 0.95 um stub = 6.3e-10 cm2, so J=1e-7 A/cm2 -> 0.063 fA/cell vs 13 fA (64 ms), 0.84 fA (1 s), 0.084 fA (10 s); J=1e-5 -> 6.3 fA still meets 64 ms. So a Si-BCAT DRAM tolerates J up to ~1e-5 at the storage bias, while a 10 s oxide-channel cell needs <=~1e-7 at ~0.5 V. Sn use: 0.44 g/wafer at 15% ALD utilization -> ~10 t/yr fleet = ~0.003% of world tin [world tin UNVERIFIED-PK].

ideas.name: Hf-free MPB zirconia with work-function-biased operating point
ideas.one_liner: Reach k ~55-60 without hafnium by tuning Zr-only ZrO2 stacks to the tetragonal/polar-orthorhombic boundary and using asymmetric electrodes to park the DRAM operating window on the steep part of the permittivity curve.
ideas.mechanism: Today's DRAM uses Al-doped ZrO2 (k ~40, EOT ~0.6-0.7 nm). The highest reported hafnia-zirconia k values (56-64) sit at the morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) between ferroelectric-orthorhombic and tetragonal phases, using HZO superlattices that contain Hf. Here the stack is Zr-only ZrO2 (5.5-6 nm) whose phase balance is set by dopant (Al, Si, Y), thickness and electrode strain. An antiferroelectric-like ZrO2 has its highest small-signal permittivity near its field-induced transition; a built-in bias from work-function-asymmetric electrodes (TiN bottom, doped-SnO2 or MoO2 top) shifts that peak into the 0-0.5 V storage window. The capacitor is otherwise a standard pillar or stub.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 capacitor wall; A2 Hf warning (HZO fleet-wide = 14-41% of separated world Hf; Hf price ~$5k -> ~$13k/kg in 2025-26).
ideas.step_change_claim: EOT 0.55 -> ~0.41 nm (k 40 -> 56): the same 5.4 fF from a 0.97 um pillar instead of 1.29 um (AR 62 -> 46), or +34% Cs at the same height, Hf-free. A modest step on its own; it compounds with B2-01 (taller AAO cups) or B2-08 (shorter bitlines).
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-03: k=40 at 5.6 nm -> EOT 0.546 nm -> h=1.29 um (AR 62); k=56 at 5.9 nm -> 0.411 nm -> 0.97 um (AR 46); k=62 -> 0.371 nm -> 0.88 um (AR 42), all at d=21 nm and 5.4 fF. Zr demand is unchanged from today (~19 t/yr fleet, <0.01% of Zr, A2).

(3) Laminate with thin Al2O3 for leakage and use oxidation-tolerant oxide top electrodes.

ideas.name: Capacitor-first inverted flow with perovskite super-k
ideas.one_liner: Build and crystallize a perovskite (Ba,Sr)TiO3 capacitor array at 650-750 C before any transistor exists, then grow low-temperature oxide access transistors on top and bond the periphery last, so the thermal-budget conflict that killed perovskite DRAM disappears.
ideas.mechanism: On a bare carrier or Si wafer, deposit a conductive-oxide bottom electrode (LaNiO3, Nb:SrTiO3 or doped SnO2), sputter/ALD 10-12 nm (Ba,Sr)TiO3 or SrTiO3 into short pillars or cups, and RTA at 650-750 C to crystallize (k 100-250); add the top electrode and planarize. Then build vertical IGZO/ZTO access transistors directly on the capacitor top contacts at <=400 C (the OCTRAM-style transistor-over-capacitor arrangement), and finally hybrid-bond the logic periphery wafer on top. Because the capacitor comes first, no transistor, metal or gate stack ever sees the perovskite anneal. The bit is a normal 1T1C charge sensed through a short bitline.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 (k>=100 needed for a <=300-500 nm capacitor), A1 #2 (a stub that fits a tier), A1 #4 (HAR etch).
ideas.step_change_claim: 3-4x shorter capacitor at equal charge: k 150 (EOT 0.26 nm) gives 4.6 fF from a 0.5 um stub (vs 5.4 fF from 1.3 um today), AR ~23 instead of 60-75; a 0.3 um stub gives 1.8-3.8 fF, enough for 64-128-cell bitlines.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-04 (d=22 nm pillar at a 40 nm-pitch 4F2 lattice): k=100/10 nm (EOT 0.39) -> 1.84 fF at 0.3 um, 3.06 fF at 0.5 um; k=150/10 nm (EOT 0.26) -> 2.75/4.59 fF; k=250/12 nm (EOT 0.19) -> 3.82/6.37 fF. Leakage: SrTiO3 at EOT 0.42 nm showed ~1e-6 A/cm2 (A1 cross-ref); over a 0.5 um stub's 3.5e-10 cm2 that is ~0.35 fA, acceptable for 64 ms-1 s retention but not for 10 s.

ideas.novelty: NEW combination: process-order inversion (capacitor-first, high-temperature perovskite) enabled only by oxide-channel transistors plus bonded periphery. Perovskite (BST) DRAM capacitors were pursued in the 1990s-2000s and abandoned over integration and electrodes [UNVERIFIED-PK]. That OCTRAM places the IGZO transistor above the capacitor is from prior knowledge [UNVERIFIED-PK].
ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Thin-film perovskite k collapses (dead layers, grain size vs a 22 nm pillar) and leaks (~3.2 eV gap). (2) Electrodes: oxidation-resistant contacts are traditionally Pt/Ru/SrRuO3 (scarce); LaNiO3 needs La (China-processed rare earth). (3) Conformal perovskite deposition in 3D (Ba/Sr ALD precursors are poor) and interdiffusion during the anneal.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Target the short-stub regime (AR <=25), where sputter or ALD/sputter hybrids suffice, and accept 64 ms-1 s retention products; Al2O3 interlayers for leakage. (2) LaNiO3 from Mountain Pass (U.S.) lanthanum or doped-SnO2 electrodes; no Ru. (3) Crystallize planar or shallow-cup capacitors first; the transistor-on-top flow needs no conformal 60:1 coating.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 18 months, ~$300k: planar and 300-500 nm cup BST/STO capacitors on LaNiO3 at 650-750 C; then a <=350 C IGZO TFT on top; measure C, J, k vs thickness and 1T1C retention at 85 C. Pass bar: >=2 fF from a <=0.5 um cup at J <=1e-6 A/cm2 and 0.5 V.

ideas.name: Solid-state proton double-layer nano-capacitor [SPECULATIVE]
ideas.one_liner: Store the DRAM charge in an electric double layer across a few-nm solid proton electrolyte (phosphosilicate glass), which holds 2-16x more charge per area than ZrO2, so a 0.1-0.4 um stub replaces a 1.3 um pillar.
ideas.mechanism: Replace the high-k film with a 3-5 nm PECVD phosphosilicate-glass (PSG) proton conductor between ion-blocking TiN or W electrodes, optionally with a 1-2 nm pseudocapacitive WO3 or MnO2 skin. Applying the bit voltage (<=~1 V) moves protons a fraction of a nm to form double layers at both interfaces: an all-solid-state nano-supercapacitor with ~10-20 uF/cm2 (EDL) or ~100 uF/cm2 (pseudocapacitive) vs 6.3 uF/cm2 for EOT 0.55 nm. The access transistor and sensing are unchanged. MIT showed nanosecond proton shuttling through PSG at room temperature under ~1 V/nm fields.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 capacitor wall (charge per footprint), A1 #2 (capacitor in a tier).
ideas.step_change_claim: 5.4 fF from a 0.41 um stub (EDL, 20 uF/cm2) or 0.08 um (pseudocapacitive, 100 uF/cm2) at 21 nm diameter, vs 1.3 um today: 3-16x shorter, with all-abundant P/Si/O/H/W.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-05: ZrO2-class EOT 0.55 nm = 6.28 uF/cm2. Height for 5.4 fF at d=21 nm: 10 uF/cm2 -> 0.82 um, 20 -> 0.41 um, 100 -> 0.08 um. Speed: R_ion = t/(sigma*A) for a 5 nm film over 2.7e-10 cm2: sigma 1e-3 S/cm -> RC 10 ns, 1e-4 -> 100 ns, 1e-5 -> 1 us. DRAM-class write needs effective sigma >=1e-3 S/cm, plausible only in the high-field regime MIT reported. Retention: electronic leakage at 1e-6 A/cm2 over 2.7e-10 cm2 = 0.27 fA (meets 64 ms and 1 s).

ideas.name: Flat AlBN ferroelectric capacitor with non-destructive capacitive read
ideas.one_liner: Use Sc-free, Hf-free boron-aluminum nitride, whose remanent polarization (~125-136 uC/cm2) is ~5x hafnia's, to store a full DRAM bit's charge in a flat 20-40 nm capacitor with no height at all, and read it without switching.
ideas.mechanism: Sputter 5-10 nm wurtzite Al1-xBxN (x 0.02-0.15) at <=400 C on a planar landing pad: 2Pr*A for a 40x40 nm pad is ~4 fC (~26,000 e-), more than today's 1.3 um pillar delivers. Reads must not switch the film, so the state is read capacitively: the imprinted polarization gives different small-signal C (or a piezo/flexo-induced charge) for up and down states, sensed through a 2T gain cell on an oxide channel, so only writes wear the ferroelectric. Data are non-volatile: no refresh. A gain-cell or SRAM write buffer in front absorbs write traffic.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #1 (removes the HAR capacitor), A1 #3 (no refresh), A2 (AlScN on 3D area would need ~13% of world Sc; HZO 14-41% of Hf).
ideas.step_change_claim: Zero capacitor height and zero refresh energy; 1-4 fC per bit from a planar 20-40 nm pad; Sc- and Hf-free. Gated by an endurance gap of ~1e5-1e9x.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-06: 2Pr*A: Pr=130 uC/cm2, 20x20 nm -> 1.04 fC (6,492 e-); 40x40 nm -> 4.16 fC (25,968 e-); HZO-class Pr=25 at 20x20 nm -> 0.20 fC. Coercive voltage = Ec*t: 5.4 MV/cm x 5 nm = 2.7 V; with B+Sc co-alloys at 3 MV/cm, 5 nm -> 1.5 V. Endurance: >1e6 demonstrated vs ~3.4e15 needed for DRAM-class (3.4e9x) or 1.6e11 for a write-buffered tier (1.6e5x).

ideas.name: Gallium-free, indium-lean oxide channels (ZTO / SnO2 / ITZO) for gain cells and VCT
ideas.one_liner: Make the oxide-channel DRAM wave independent of China-controlled gallium (and mostly of indium) by switching IGZO/IGO channels to zinc-tin oxide or In-lean tin oxides; Ga-free ZTO 2T0C already holds data >1500 s.
ideas.mechanism: Deposit amorphous Zn-Sn-O (ZTO), SnO2, or In-lean In-Sn-Zn-O / In-W-O channels by ALD (or PVD for planar) at <=350 C, with the gate insulator and channel grown in one ALD chamber without a vacuum break (UMich) and Al2O3/SiO2 passivation (Hf-free, unlike the HfO2 used for the SJTU record). Cells are the same 2T0C/3T0C gain cells or 4F2 VCT access transistors now built with IGZO. Zn and Sn suppress oxygen-vacancy carriers less strongly than Ga, so thin (3-5 nm) channels, Al or Si doping, and O3 anneals set the threshold voltage. The bit is stored on the read transistor's gate (gain cell) or on a capacitor (VCT).
ideas.which_bottleneck: A2 chokepoint: Ga is ~98% Chinese and the U.S. export-ban suspension ends 2026-11-27; In refining is concentrated. Keeps A1 #3 (oxide leakage -> long retention).
ideas.step_change_claim: 100% Ga-free (and In-free for ZTO) oxide DRAM supply chain at >=1500 s demonstrated retention (~23,000x a 64 ms refresh interval), with 2-6 ns single-bit read on a 64-cell read bitline.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-07: read bitline C = 0.1 fF/cell + 5 fF (A3); 64 cells = 11.4 fF. 100 mV develops in t = C*dV/I: 0.2 uA (ZTO at ~1/3 of IGZO drive) -> 5.7 ns; 0.6 uA -> 1.9 ns; 3-bit (8x) -> 15-46 ns. Retention 1500 s / 64 ms = 23,400x, so refresh energy falls in proportion. Material per wafer is mg-scale (A2: IGZO uses 26 mg In and 16 mg Ga per wafer; ZTO replaces both with Zn and Sn).

ideas.name: In-tier complementary-oxide sense amplifiers (no-bond short bitlines)
ideas.one_liner: Use the new p-type oxides (TeSeOx, SnO) with n-IGZO/ZTO to build local sense amps as a BEOL tier right next to each memory tier group, so every 64-cell bitline segment gets its own amplifier without wafer bonding.
ideas.mechanism: Build complementary oxide TFT latch sense amplifiers (n-IGZO/ZTO + p-TeSeOx, mobility ~15 cm2/Vs, on/off 1e6-1e7) in a dedicated BEOL tier above or below the memory tier(s), connected by short vias to 64-cell local bitline segments. Short bitlines (Cbl ~8 fF instead of ~35 fF) cut the needed storage capacitance to ~1.2 fF and allow VARY ~0.4 V; the local SA restores the cell and drives a global bitline to the Si periphery. In 3D stacks one SA tier serves N memory tiers, so bitline capacitance no longer grows with tier count. Offset-cancelled (auto-zero) SA topology absorbs oxide Vt mismatch.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #10 voltage floor, A1 #1 (Cs requirement), A1 #7 periphery area (~49% of the die), A1 #2 (bitline routing in 3D).
ideas.step_change_claim: ~27x lower bitline CV2/2 energy per sense (17.5 -> 0.64 fJ) and ~4.5x lower Cs requirement (5.4 -> ~1.2 fF), monolithically, without a second bonded wafer.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-08: 512-cell BL 35 fF at 1.0 V -> 17.5 fJ; 64-cell 8 fF at 0.4 V -> 0.64 fJ (27x). Area: a 64-cell segment at 4F2 F=20 nm covers 0.102 um2, so an open-BL SA serving two segments gets 0.205 um2 per tier; stacked over 4/8/16 tiers it gets 0.82/1.64/3.28 um2. Offset: oxide sigma(Vt) ~40 mV [ASSUMPTION] -> 6-sigma pair offset ~339 mV, above the 215 mV fresh 64-cell signal (A1), so offset cancellation is mandatory.

ideas.name: Ge-free, NAND-line 3D oxide gain cell (oxide/nitride mold + channel replacement)
ideas.one_liner: Build 3D DRAM the way 3D NAND is built (deposited SiO2/SiN mold, one hole etch, replacement), with capacitorless oxide gain cells, instead of epitaxial Si/SiGe superlattices that need germanium and single-crystal tiers.
ideas.mechanism: Deposit 16-64 SiO2/SiN pairs by PECVD (standard NAND tools). One HAR hole/slit etch exposes all tiers; SiN is removed with hot phosphoric acid and replaced in every tier by ALD IGZO/ZTO horizontal channels (Kioxia's 3D OCTRAM SiN->InGaZnO replacement) plus recessed W/Mo gate and storage-node fills. Vertical wordline pillars gate the write transistors through all tiers (IMECAS dual-gate vertical-WL 2T0C); each storage node is a metal island that gates the tier's read transistor, so no lateral capacitor is needed. 2-3 bits/cell with write-verify multiplies the tier count.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #2 (no manufacturable 3D DRAM cell), A1 #4 (bits by deposition, not lithography); A2: Si/SiGe superlattices fleet-wide need 6-38% of refined world Ge; reuses NAND capital and cleanroom.
ideas.step_change_claim: 1.1-3.4x 1-beta density at F=40 nm with 16 tiers (1-3 bits), 6.8x at 32 tiers x 3 bits, with no EUV, no Ge and no epitaxy; runs on 3D-NAND tool sets.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-09 (vertical 2T0C 10F2, eff 0.508, A3 convention): F=40, 1 b x 16 tiers -> 0.51 Gb/mm2 (1.1x); 3 b x 16 -> 1.52 (3.4x); 3 b x 32 -> 3.05 (6.8x); F=30, 2 b x 32 -> 3.61 (8.1x). Ge avoided: 9-53 t/yr fleet-wide (A2). Tier break-even per A1 is ~26 for a capacitor-bearing 1T1C; deleting the capacitor drops it to the 10F2 footprint.

ideas.name: Fluorine-free carbon mold for capacitor holes and sacrificial 3D tiers
ideas.one_liner: Make the HAR molds out of amorphous carbon, etched with O2/COS or H2/N2 plasma and removed by oxygen, so the largest-volume HAR etches in DRAM need no fluorocarbon (PFAS-class) gas at all.
ideas.mechanism: Replace the SiO2 capacitor mold with a 1.3-2.5 um PECVD amorphous-carbon film (the 3D-NAND hardmask material) capped by a thin SiN or Al2O3 support lattice. Holes are etched anisotropically in O2/COS or H2/N2 plasma (sulfur or nitrogen sidewall passivation, no fluorine). ALD electrode and dielectric (or oxide channel) fill the holes; the carbon is then burned out by O2 or removed by H2 plasma, leaving free-standing, lattice-supported structures. In 3D stacks, carbon replaces SiN as the sacrificial tier: a low-pressure thermal O2 burn is reaction-limited, so the lateral recess is uniform from top to bottom of the stack, and the product is CO2.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A2 PFAS/fluorochemical chokepoint (EU restriction ~2028+, 3M exit); A1 #1/#2 HAR etch and 3D lateral-recess uniformity.
ideas.step_change_claim: Eliminates fluorocarbon gas from the capacitor/channel-hole modules (~5.6e13 HAR holes per wafer at 1-beta) and makes 3D lateral recess a thermal, reaction-limited step; the mold leaves ~0.6 g CO2/wafer instead of PFAS-class by-products.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-10: one capacitor hole per 1,070 nm2 cell -> 9.35e8 holes/mm2 -> 5.6e13 per wafer. A 1.3 um a-C mold (1.8 g/cm3) is 0.17 g C per wafer -> 0.61 g CO2 on burn-out. The low-GWP replacements under study (C2F4O: -24-29% GWP; HFO-1234ze) are still fluorinated, so this is a 100% rather than a 25% cut for these steps.

ideas.name: DSA honeycomb: block-copolymer self-assembly for the capacitor/channel hole lattice
ideas.one_liner: The hexagonal lattice that cylinder-forming block copolymers assemble into is the DRAM capacitor honeycomb; register it with a relaxed ArF guide and let thermodynamics do the EUV's job.
ideas.mechanism: Coat PS-b-PMMA (or a high-chi BCP for <30 nm) whose cylinder lattice period L0 (~28-40 nm) matches the 1-beta (35 nm) or 1c (32 nm) capacitor honeycomb. A single-exposure ArF immersion guide pattern (or chemical pre-pattern) at 2-3x the pitch registers the lattice and DSA multiplies density 3-4x, rectifying CD and placement noise. Sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O into PMMA) hardens the pattern into an AlOx mask for transfer into the mold (SiO2 or the carbon mold of B2-10). For 4F2 square lattices, chemo-epitaxy with a square guide is used.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #4 litho-bound scaling and EUV dependence; A2 EUV single-supplier chokepoint.
ideas.step_change_claim: Replaces 1-2 EUV or SAQP layers in the array: $165-330 per wafer (3.8-7.7% of a $4.3k 1c wafer) before netting DSA cost; the hole lattice comes from polymer physics rather than wavelength.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-11..14: removing 1/2/3 EUV layers saves $165/330/495 per wafer = 3.8/7.7/11.5% of a 1c wafer. Lattice match: imec used a 37 nm-pitch BCP for contact-hole multiplication (BACUS 2014); 1-beta honeycomb 35 nm, 1c 32 nm (A1). A guide at ~70-105 nm pitch is single-exposure ArF immersion territory (no multipatterning).

ideas.name: NIL-only periodic cell wafer (bonded periphery makes every layer imprintable)
ideas.one_liner: Once the periphery lives on a separate bonded logic wafer, the cell wafer contains only perfectly periodic arrays, which is exactly what nanoimprint does best, so pattern every critical cell layer by imprint and drop EUV and SAQP from it.
ideas.mechanism: A master template (e-beam- or DSA-written) is replicated into working templates; jet-and-flash imprint defines each field's hole or line lattice with no projection optics. Because the cell wafer of a bonded 4F2 VCT or vertical gain-cell array needs only 2-3 overlay-critical layers (channel holes, wordline, contact) and later layers self-align, NIL's overlay and pattern-variety weaknesses matter less. 3D templates can define line + contact in a single imprint (dual-damascene style). Defects are absorbed by redundancy and ECC (B2-15).
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #4 (EUV, capex, depreciation ~55% of wafer cost), A2 EUV single supplier (~65 tools/yr, ~10 GWh/yr each).
ideas.step_change_claim: No EUV and no SAQP spacer loops on array layers: 2-3 imprint layers replace ~4-6 EUV/SAQP-patterned layers [ESTIMATE], worth ~$330-500/wafer at EUV rates; litho tool capex per wafer start plausibly several-fold lower [UNVERIFIED-PK on tool price].
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-11..14: 2-3 EUV layers at $165 = $330-495/wafer (7.7-11.5% of a 1c wafer). Overlay budget for DRAM critical layers = 15-20% of half pitch (NIL review): at F=20 nm that is 3-4 nm, about 1.4x looser than at 14 nm (2.1-2.8 nm).

ideas.name: Maskless interference lithography for an all-periodic cell wafer
ideas.one_liner: Pattern the periphery-free cell wafer with two-beam 193 nm immersion interference fringes (no mask, no projection lens): ~35 nm half-pitch lines, crossed for hole lattices, one spacer step to F~17 nm 4F2.
ideas.mechanism: Two (or four) coherent 193 nm beams interfere in water immersion to write a fringe pattern at half-pitch ~34.5-36 nm; two crossed exposures give post or hole lattices at ~70 nm pitch, and one SADP halves that to ~35 nm. Scanning-beam interference lithography (Doppler writing) phase-locks the fringe to wafer marks for overlay and covers 300 mm continuously. Array edges and the few non-periodic features are cut by a coarse KrF/i-line trim exposure whose overlay is not critical. Possible only because bonded periphery has removed all random logic from the cell wafer.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #4 (litho capex, EUV), A2 EUV single-supplier chokepoint and capital per bit.
ideas.step_change_claim: No masks and no EUV for array layers; 4F2 at F~17-18 nm with one SADP; litho tool capex estimated ~10x below an ArF immersion scanner and ~50-100x below EUV [ESTIMATE: no projection optics].
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-13: hp = lambda/(4 n sin(theta)) = 193/(4 x 1.44 x 0.93-0.97) = 34.5-36.0 nm (Brueck patent gives ~33.5 nm limit); crossed exposures -> 69-72 nm-pitch posts; +SADP -> ~35 nm pitch -> 4F2 1T1C at F=17.3-18 nm = 1,197-1,296 nm2/cell -> 0.54-0.58 Gb/mm2 at array eff 0.70 (1.2-1.3x 1-beta) with no EUV and no masks on the array. RIT reached 38 nm hp at NA 1.25; Lincoln Lab 22 nm hp at 157 nm.

ideas.name: ASD self-aligned landing pads and top contacts
ideas.one_liner: Grow the storage-node landing pads and vertical-channel top contacts bottom-up by area-selective deposition so they self-align to the plugs below and a dedicated critical lithography layer disappears.
ideas.mechanism: After the contact plugs are exposed in dielectric, Mo (or W) is deposited by area-selective ALD/CVD that nucleates only on metal or semiconductor surfaces, with small-molecule or SAM inhibitors on the dielectric and periodic atomic-layer-etch 'defect clean' cycles to remove stray nuclei. The pad grows a controlled height and mushroom width, self-aligned to its plug, so the landing-pad litho/etch step (patterned with EUV or multipatterning at leading nodes [UNVERIFIED-PK]) is not needed. The same approach caps vertical oxide channels in 4F2 VCT and gain-cell arrays.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #4 masks/EUV; A1 #2 (self-aligned contacts in 3D); A2 tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%).
ideas.step_change_claim: -1 to -2 critical litho layers (~$165-330/wafer if EUV-patterned; 3.8-7.7% of a 1c wafer) and fewer fluorocarbon etches; Mo replaces WF6-based W.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-11..14 for the layer cost. Selectivity requirement: with ~1.7e10 pads per 16 Gb die and repair able to handle ~1e4-1e5 random fails (more with B2-15), the stray-nucleus bridging probability must be <=1e-6-1e-5 per pad gap. Mushroom growth = pad thickness, so a 15 nm gap allows <=7 nm of over-growth per side.

ideas.name: Defect-budget co-design: 100x pattern-defect tolerance to unlock cheap patterning
ideas.one_liner: Specify the array to survive a 1e-4 random cell-defect fraction (vs ~1e-6 assumed today) with t=2 BCH ECC in the logic periphery and a tiny remap table, so NIL, DSA, interference litho, AAO and panel processes become usable.
ideas.mechanism: Every 128-bit word carries 16 BCH (t=2) check bits instead of 8 SECDED bits, decoded in fast logic-process periphery (bonded or under-array). A small CAM remaps the few residual failing words found at test; mat-level sparing (NAND bad-block style) handles clustered pattern defects (line opens, shorts). Retention-weak cells are remapped too. This turns patterning defectivity from a yield killer into a few percent of area overhead.
ideas.which_bottleneck: Enabling layer for A1 #4 (cheap patterning) and A1 #2 (3D tier yield ~0.998/tier needed); A2 capital per bit.
ideas.step_change_claim: Random-defect tolerance x100 (p 1e-6 -> 1e-4) for +6.25% extra check bits and ~65 remap words per 16 Gb die.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-15 (16 Gb die, 1.34e8 words of 128 bits): p=1e-4 -> 1.72M defective cells; SECDED (136,128) failing words = C(136,2) p^2 x words ~12,336; BCH t=2 (144,128) failing words = C(144,3) p^3 x words ~65. At p=1e-5: 123 vs 0.1. The ECC must also cover soft errors and retention tails, so the defect budget is set at ~1e-4, not higher.

ideas.name: Main memory inside the logic die's own metal stack (monolithic BEOL oxide gain cells)
ideas.one_liner: Build 8-16 tiers of 3-bit oxide gain cells directly in the upper BEOL of the GPU/CPU die at <=400 C, putting tens of GB of DRAM-class memory microns from the compute with no DRAM wafer, no TSVs and no HBM stack.
ideas.mechanism: After the logic metal stack is complete (TSMC has already embedded an oxide-semiconductor-selector memory fully in BEOL above advanced logic), deposit 8-16 tiers of vertical IGZO/ZTO 2T0C cells with 3 bits/cell write-verify, local complementary-oxide sensing (B2-08) and short vias down to SRAM-buffered memory controllers. Oxide cells retain >200 s at 95 C, so they tolerate sitting on hot logic. On backside-power logic, the frontside BEOL is less congested. Capacity is the target, not cache: an 800 mm2 die area carries 76-152 GB.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #5 interface energy (HBM ~3-4 pJ/bit), A1 #6 HBM TSV tax (~3x wafer per bit), A1 #3 (hot retention); A2 prime wafers and HPQ crucibles.
ideas.step_change_claim: 76-152 GB over an 800 mm2 die (3 b x 8-16 tiers at F=40 nm, no EUV); interface energy 3.5 -> ~0.2 pJ/bit, saving 211-422 W per accelerator at 8-16 TB/s; zero extra wafers; added cost ~$0.87/GB at $500 per tier per wafer and 80% yield.

ideas.name: Self-assembled tier stack: parallel block-copolymer lamellae + sequential infiltration synthesis [SPECULATIVE]
ideas.one_liner: Spin one micron-thick block-copolymer film that self-organizes into 25-80 substrate-parallel layers, convert alternate layers to AlOx by vapor infiltration, and use it as the 3D mold: tens of tiers from one coat instead of tens of PECVD depositions.
ideas.mechanism: A lamella-forming BCP (L0 25-40 nm) with preferential wetting on both interfaces orders parallel to the substrate after annealing, giving 25-80 alternating layers in a 1-2 um film. Sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O) converts the PMMA layers into AlOx sheets; the PS layers remain as sacrificial carbon tiers (removed later by oxidation, as in B2-10). A single hole etch then opens all tiers; lateral recess and ALD oxide-channel/gate fills proceed as in B2-09. Tier thickness is set by polymer molecular weight rather than deposition time.
ideas.which_bottleneck: A1 #2 (tier cost and count for 3D DRAM), A2 capital and cleanroom time (PECVD stack deposition is a long, tool-heavy step).
ideas.step_change_claim: 25-80 tiers per coat vs one PECVD pair per tier: tier-formation tool time ~10-50x lower [ESTIMATE]; no SiN/SiGe stack.
ideas.first_principles_estimate: models/B2_materials_estimates.py B2-20: periods = film thickness / L0: L0 25 nm -> 40 (1 um) or 80 (2 um) tiers; L0 40 nm -> 25-50 tiers. Tier-thickness tolerance ~+/-1 nm (4% of 25 nm) is needed; L0 scales ~N^(2/3), so molecular-weight dispersity sets the floor [UNVERIFIED-PK].

ideas.show_stoppers: (1) Long-range parallel order with +/-1 nm layer uniformity through a micron-thick film; dislocations and undulations. (2) Mechanics and thermal stability: AlOx sheets need supports; polymers survive only ~250-300 C before conversion. (3) SIS penetration depth in thick films.
ideas.revival_or_workaround: (1) Coat 8-16 periods at a time and repeat; high-chi, low-dispersity BCPs; crosslinkable blocks. (2) Convert fully to inorganic (AlOx/carbon) before any ALD; add support pillars in the first hole etch. (3) Long-exposure or pressure-pulsed SIS; thinner sub-stacks.
ideas.million_dollar_demo: 12 months, ~$150k: 10-20-period parallel lamellae on 100 mm wafers; SIS conversion; cross-section TEM layer-thickness statistics; one hole etch and ALD IGZO into the recesses; a single-tier transistor test.
ideas.resource_angle: Replaces dozens of SiH4/TEOS/NH3 PECVD steps with one coat plus vapor infiltration; lower energy and tool time; commodity polymers (solvent use instead of dry deposition).
